newsletter_description: Explore the paradox of being seen vs. seized in the 'Looking For Terry' exhibition.
description: Group Exhibition "Looking For Terry" examines the paradox of being seen versus seized through the legal framework of the Terry stop. Historically, this language has functioned as a mechanism of racialized looking, rendering Black bodies hyper-visible to surveillance while obscuring their interior lives. Rather than rehearsing scenes of policing, the exhibition turns inward, attending to the psychic and emotional terrain shaped by the knowledge of being perpetually subject to scrutiny. Black interiority emerges as a site of vulnerability and quiet resistance. Memory, abstraction, and opacity operate as strategies of self-definition, resisting demands for legibility within systems that equate visibility with control. The works gathered cultivate atmospheres of reflection and ambiguity, inviting a slower mode of looking—one that honors complexity without disclosure. In Looking for Terry, to be seen is not to be seized. Opacity becomes an ethical stance, affirming that Black life exceeds the frames through which it has too often been searched.

newsletter_description: Apply for the Diamond Foundation Scholarships to support your educational journey!
description: The Diamond Foundation Inc. is accepting applications for its 2026 scholarships. This philanthropic arm of the New Brunswick Alumni chapter of Kappa Alpha Psi Fraternity, Inc. focuses on providing educational opportunities for students of color with the goal of supporting the development of tomorrow’s minority leaders. The scholarship award is between $1500 and $2500. Requirements include being a graduating high school senior from Middlesex or Somerset counties planning to attend a four-year college or university, submitting a high school transcript, two letters of recommendation, a completed scholarship application including an essay, and a photograph.

event_name: Midnight Market at LSC After Dark
newsletter_description: Experience $5 bites and a lively nightlife at Liberty Science Center with Midnight Market!
description: Midnight Market brought its signature $5 food festival experience to Liberty Science Center during LSC After Dark, blending a range of food vendors with a lively nightlife atmosphere. The 21+ event featured a lineup of vendors serving $5 bites, allowing guests to try multiple dishes throughout the night without the high cost typically associated with dining out. A live DJ kept the energy up as guests filled the dance floor and made their way from vendor to vendor, trying different dishes, drinks, and sharing bites along the way. In addition to the market, attendees explored exhibits throughout the science center and experienced a planetarium show, adding an interactive element to the night.

newsletter_description: Join the DCR and Newark Public Library for a summit on housing post-incarceration.
description: The New Jersey Division on Civil Rights and Newark Public Library are proud to bring together justice‑impacted individuals, service providers, advocates, and all who believe in the right to live free from discrimination. Stable housing is essential for success after incarceration — yet formerly incarcerated people are nearly 10x more likely to experience homelessness. Join us to learn about DCR’s work supporting people with justice‑involved backgrounds, hear powerful firsthand stories, and connect with communities committed to second chances and civil rights.

newsletter_description: Taste the best Spudnuts in Morristown at Verrilli's!
description: The oldest standing business in Morristown may just have the best donuts we’ve ever tasted. Because if these Spudnuts qualify as donuts, I’m calling them a win. SPUDNUTS are donuts made with potatoes (don’t ask us how because we don’t know) and they are the BESTEST. They are like zeppoles on crack. We are obsessed. And do not sleep on the butter glaze. OMG. Since @verrillispizzaandbakery is also known for their food, we will be back for more and will definitely save room for dessert. Owned by two families since they opened, @verrillispizzaandbakery is an icon and a community hub. Owner Kristi Dimogerodakis bought it from the original family when they decided to sell. It was 1988. She was 18. She’s still there behind the counter, talking and baking and laughing and WE LOVE HER. Thank you @alidamic0 and @ka_lang for recommending it. We are really addicted to those spudnuts and that place. (They also have outdoor seating in good weather so go spend some time.)

event_name: Jersey City Board of Education Caucus
newsletter_description: Tempers flare at the Jersey City Board of Education caucus with a speaker removed from the meeting.
description: Tempers flared at Tuesday’s Jersey City Board of Education caucus when the board’s vice president cut a former school district clerk’s remarks short and ordered her removed from the meeting. The ex-employee, Mary Cordero, attempted to speak during public comment about a remark Board President Noemí Velázquez made at February’s board meeting. Velázquez said Trustee Lorenzo Richardson, who is Black and was dressed in traditional African garb, was “looking like somebody who’s coming to America” — a reference to a 1988 Eddie Murphy film. Richardson called the comment disrespectful and racist, and Velázquez later publicly apologized. “I have come out of forced retirement to address the bigotry and divisive actions of this school board,” Cordero said at Tuesday’s caucus meeting. Velázquez left the room a few seconds after Cordero began speaking, leaving Morris temporarily in charge. A minute into Cordero’s remarks, shortly after she used the term “crap show,” Morris banged Velázquez’s gavel, and the board’s attorney advised Cordero that speakers must refrain from using “crude or obscene” language. Morris warned her that if she violated the public comment policy again, he would cut her speaking time short. Cordero continued with her remarks, but after she said that Superintendent Norma Fernandez has watched as Velázquez’s “bigotry has reared its ugly head,” Morris banged the gavel again. Cordero asked what she had said that violated the comment policy, but Morris did not answer. When Cordero continued to stand at the podium and vocally protest, Morris told her she was trespassing and motioned for the school district’s security director to escort her from the room. As she was leaving, Cordero shouted: “First Amendment! That’s why you were let go from being a cop. You’re a bad person. I’ll say it on Facebook, and TikTok, and everywhere else, because I’ve got to state the truth.”

description:
From 1984 through 1993, John Lee was Dizzy Gillespie’s bassist. Currently, he serves as both bassist and director for the Dizzy Gillespie All-Stars, the Dizzy Gillespie All-Star Big Band, and the Dizzy Gillespie Afro-Latin Experience. John’s distinguished career has seen him perform and collaborate with renowned artists including Gary Bartz, Larry Coryell, Jon Faddis, Aretha Franklin, Roberta Gambarini, Roy Hargrove, Jimmy Heath, Gregory Hines, Miriam Makeba, James Moody, Claudio Roditi, Sonny Rollins, and McCoy Tyner. A Grammy-winning record producer and audio engineer, John has produced more than 100 recordings. He also co-founded the Jazz Legacy Productions (JLP) label.

Seatings at 6:15 and 8:35, $40 food & drink minimum per person. $8 entertainment fee. Reservations strongly recommended.
